en.title: Minimum Cost to Equalize a Ring Moving in One Direction Only
en.description:
n containers form a ring, and all products must end up evenly distributed among the containers; the total is guaranteed to be divisible by n. Moving one product across one adjacent edge costs 1. The whole process may use only one direction, clockwise or counterclockwise; either direction may be chosen, but they cannot be mixed. Find the minimum cost.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the product counts. The original snapshot gave no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, counts 0..10^9, and a total divisible by n.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: the prefix surpluses are −2, −3, −2, −1, 0; the clockwise cost is 7 and the counterclockwise cost is 8, so the answer is 7. Example 2: already evenly distributed, cost 0. Example 3: send 1 product across one edge to the empty container, cost 1.
hints: Compute the prefix surplus P of each container relative to the average. The clockwise cost is sum(P)−n min(P) and the counterclockwise cost is n max(P)−sum(P); take the smaller one.
